A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same research work, with matching title, authors, and theoretical development. All 24 pages of each were inspected through text extraction and rendered-page comparison. Neither contains a separate appendix; both end with references. No material gaps limit comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports theoretical bounds, proofs, and illustrative mathematical constructions in Sections 4–6. It contains no original experimental, simulation, user-study, or data-analysis results.

after.justification: v3 retains the same theoretical results and examples, with expanded related work. No original empirical results appear anywhere in the PDF.

M1.justification: The min-max ERM algorithm in Section 4.1, including its error estimates and predictor-selection objective, is unchanged.

E1.justification: Neither version uses datasets for empirical training or evaluation. Binary classification and the theoretical extensions to multiclass classification and regression in Remark 4.2 are unchanged.

E2.justification: Neither version empirically evaluates comparison methods. The added meta-learning citations in Section 1.2 are related-work references, with no accompanying baseline evaluations.

E3.justification: Neither version reports empirical evaluation protocols. The theoretical sampling setup in Section 3 and error-estimation requirements in Section 4.1 remain unchanged.

E4.justification: No empirical ablations or robustness analyses appear in either version. The analytical ERM counterexample in Remark 4.3 and illustrative domain families in Examples 6.1–6.2 are unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental runs, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The probability guarantees in the theoretical analysis are unchanged.

E6.justification: No empirical result entries are added, removed, or revised. The theoretical bounds, numerical toy examples, and reported findings also match.

T1.justification: The definitions, assumptions, theorems, and proofs in Sections 2–6 are unchanged, including the domain sample-complexity bounds, VC-dimension relationship, and domain-adaptation connection.

C1.justification: The abstract and Section 1.1 retain the same contributions and learnability claims. The added related-work contrast restates the existing objective of learning one predictor that generalizes without target-task adaptation.

C2.justification: The interpretations and Section 7 limitations remain unchanged, including difficulties computing the dimension, selecting a hypothesis class, closing the upper/lower-bound gap, and incorporating unlabeled target-domain data.

D1.justification: The algorithm's sampling and error-estimation descriptions are retained. No implementation details, hyperparameters, hardware information, runtime measurements, or code/data access information are added or revised.

R1.justification: Section 1.2 adds Khodak et al. (2019, 2023) and Balcan et al. (2021) to discuss algorithmic meta-learning and distinguish its adaptation objectives from this paper's objective. It also adds Balcan et al. (2015) and broadens the shared-subspace discussion to include shared representations. These four works receive new bibliography entries.

P1.justification: Section 1.2 locally expands and rewrites the meta-learning paragraph, and the arXiv version/date stamp changes. The remaining narrative and section order are retained.

P2.justification: The expanded related-work paragraph shifts Section 2 downward on page 5 and its closing sentence onto page 6. Added references reflow pages 20–24. Neither version contains figures or tables.

improvement.justification: v3 modestly improves literature coverage and contextual clarity by acknowledging algorithmic meta-learning and explicitly explaining how its adaptation objectives differ from this paper's existing objective. This addresses a limited omission in Section 1.2 while preserving the algorithm, theoretical results, and limitations.
